route.title: Word-event superscription
route.marker: The word-event, genealogy, and date notice closes before first-person sweeping judgment speech begins at Zeph.1.2.
route.rationale: Keep the formal heading distinct from the first oracle, while requiring the full chapter-one judgment complex whenever the notice is interpreted.
route.counter: The superscription governs the whole book and therefore still requires book-level context.
route.basis: The notice has a distinct framing function and the speech beginning at 1:2 has its own repeated sweeping register.
route.guard: Do not infer authorship, date, royal ancestry, ethnicity, or canonical status from the superscription.

route.title: Programmatic sweeping judgment
route.marker: Repeated sweeping verbs expand across humans and creatures and close with a speech formula before the geographic narrowing to Judah and Jerusalem at Zeph.1.4.
route.rationale: Surface the sweeping creature register together because its repeated verb and closing formula complete before the oracle narrows to Judah and Jerusalem.
route.rejected: Zeph.1.1-Zeph.1.3; Zeph.1.2-Zeph.1.6; Separate chunks for members of the creature register
route.counter: Cutting-off language continues into 1:4, but the geographic and object narrowing is the stronger surface seam.
route.basis: The global scope and cumulative creature register form a compact programmatic oracle whose scope changes materially at 1:4.
route.guard: Do not retrieve the creature sweep as an unqualified global chronology or fulfillment claim.

route.title: Judah and Jerusalem cultic indictment
route.marker: The hand-against-Judah-and-Jerusalem declaration introduces coordinated cultic allegiance, withdrawal, and failure-to-seek accusations; the hush imperative restarts the discourse at Zeph.1.7.
route.rationale: Retain the cultic and non-seeking accusations as one localized indictment; splitting the coordinated catalogue would conceal its single geographic and rhetorical scope.
route.counter: The catalogue moves from named practices to the broader failure to seek, creating internal variation but not a stronger surface boundary.
route.basis: The coordinated indictment has one geographic scope and rhetorical function and resolves before the new hush-and-sacrifice tableau.
route.guard: Do not map the cultic catalogue onto a later community or total religious identity.

route.title: Hush, sacrifice, and punishment tableau
route.marker: The hush command and near-day declaration develop through prepared sacrifice and punishment; a WLC-family samekh follows Zeph.1.9 before the city soundscape begins at 1:10.
route.rationale: The hush command belongs with its prepared-sacrifice and punishment tableau, not as a detached silence maxim or an undifferentiated part of the entire day sequence.
route.counter: Day language continues throughout 1:10-18, requiring the larger day-complex parent.
route.basis: Imperative, sacrifice imagery, punishment catalogue, and paragraph evidence converge on a coherent local tableau.
route.guard: Do not detach the hush command as generic advice or decide the identities of sacrifice and guests.

route.title: Jerusalem soundscape and lamp search
route.marker: The in-that-day city soundscape moves through merchant lament and lamp search to the complacency saying and property reversal; the great-day refrain restarts at Zeph.1.14.
route.rationale: City cries, commercial collapse, interior lamp search, quoted complacency, and property reversal jointly carry the Jerusalem movement to the great-day restart.
route.counter: The move from public soundscape to private lamp search at 1:12 is a recoverable internal turn.
route.basis: Public cries, commercial collapse, private search, quoted complacency, and reversal comprise one citywide judgment movement.
route.guard: Do not isolate the complacency saying as a timeless proposition about divine action.

route.title: The great day poem
route.marker: The great-day restart and repeated day register escalate through battle, darkness, alarm, distress, blood, fire, and terminal closure; a WLC-family samekh follows Zeph.1.18.
route.rationale: The repeated day descriptions accumulate into one battle-and-darkness poem; the consequence stanza supplies its ending rather than a new standalone oracle.
route.counter: The consequences in 1:17-18 could be treated as a dependent concluding stanza.
route.basis: The repeated day descriptors and escalating consequences form a complete poetic movement with marked closure.
route.guard: Do not turn the great-day poem into an authorized timetable or fulfillment ruling.

route.title: Gather and seek appeal
route.marker: Repeated gathering, before, and seek expressions culminate in possible concealment; the causal nations rationale begins at Zeph.2.4.
route.rationale: Gathering urgency and the threefold seek response answer one another, so the appeal closes at possible concealment before the nations rationale begins.
route.counter: The terse wording and addressee scope of 2:1 remain translation-sensitive without changing the surface boundary.
route.basis: The imperatives and temporal urgency form a complete communal appeal and prevent 2:3 from surfacing as generic advice.
route.guard: Do not surface the seek appeal as a guaranteed concealment promise or identity definition.

route.title: Philistine coast oracle and remnant reversal
route.marker: The causal four-city catalogue at Zeph.2.4 prepares the coast woe, desolation, and Judah-remnant reversal through 2:7; Zeph.2.8 begins a new first-person hearing oracle concerning Moab and Ammon.
route.rationale: The named Philistine cities initiate the coastland judgment that resolves in Judah-remnant reversal; the 2:4 paragraph seam remains a child, not the surfaced boundary.
route.counter: The WLC-family samekh after 2:4 and fresh woe at 2:5 support a real dependent child seam; that seam is preserved as dissent rather than erased.
route.basis: Causal continuity and the coastland movement from city loss through desolation to remnant reversal outweigh the paragraph pressure to expose Zeph.2.4 independently.
route.guard: Do not use the coastland and remnant language for modern ethnicity, land, chronology, or fulfillment claims.

route.title: Moab and Ammon reproach and reversal
route.marker: First-person hearing, oath, Sodom-and-Gomorrah comparison, remnant inheritance, pride rationale, and widened worship horizon form one oracle before the direct Cush address at Zeph.2.12.
route.rationale: The widened worship horizon completes the Moab-Ammon reproach and reversal, whereas separating 2:11 would strip the oracle of its rhetorical outcome.
route.counter: Zeph.2.11 broadens beyond Moab and Ammon and could be retained as a dependent concluding horizon child.
route.basis: The widening horizon in 2:11 is the rhetorical result of the named-nations oracle rather than an unrelated maxim.
route.guard: Do not use the Sodom-Gomorrah comparison or remnant inheritance to authorize identity or land claims.

route.title: Brief Cush oracle
route.marker: The second-person Cush address and complete sword clause create a compact compass-cycle turn; the northward Assyria movement begins at Zeph.2.13.
route.rationale: Direct second-person address and the northward change make the terse Cush saying retrievable, but its nations-cycle parent remains mandatory because the unit is so compact.
route.counter: Its brevity makes isolated retrieval risky; it must retain nations-cycle hydration and cannot authorize historical or ethnic conclusions.
route.basis: Distinct direct address, named addressee, complete clause, and the geographic shift at 2:13 justify a one-verse literary unit.
route.guard: Retrieve the compact Cush oracle only with nations-cycle hydration; do not infer ethnicity or history from its address.

route.title: Nineveh desolation and taunt
route.marker: The northern turn, desolation, animal habitation, exposed architecture, proud self-speech, and passerby response close together before the WLC-family samekh after Zeph.2.15.
route.rationale: Nineveh desolation, animal habitation, exposed architecture, proud self-speech, and passerby taunt work as one northern-city oracle rather than separate image fragments.
route.counter: The city self-speech at 2:15 is a strong internal rhetorical turn.
route.basis: Desolation tableau and proud-city taunt are accusation and outcome within one named northern-city oracle.
route.guard: Do not use Nineveh parallels to decide chronology, national essence, dependence, or fulfillment.

route.title: Rebellious city woe
route.marker: The city woe, four failures, predatory leaders, treacherous prophets, profaning priests, and righteous-Yahweh contrast form one movement before the destroyed-nations example at Zeph.3.6.
route.rationale: The righteous-Yahweh contrast answers the rebellious-city and leadership accusations, so 3:5 closes the woe rather than forming an independent characterization.
route.counter: Zeph.3.5 changes from accusation to divine contrast and remains a recoverable dependent turn.
route.basis: The divine contrast in 3:5 answers the preceding leadership and cult indictment and belongs with it.
route.guard: Do not identify the accused city beyond the discourse evidence or universalize its institutional accusations.

route.title: Warning example and failed correction
route.marker: The destroyed-nations example leads to the quoted correction summons and failed response; therefore-wait-for-me pivots at Zeph.3.8.
route.rationale: Destroyed-nations example, intended correction, and corrupt response form a complete warning movement before the inferential wait summons changes function.
route.rejected: Attach Zeph.3.6-Zeph.3.7 wholly to Zeph.3.1-Zeph.3.5; Attach Zeph.3.6-Zeph.3.7 wholly to Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13; Separate the correction quotation from its failed response
route.counter: Pronoun and causal scope link the movement backward to the city woe and forward to the therefore clause.
route.basis: Example, expected correction, and failed response form a complete warning-response movement before the inferential pivot.
route.guard: Do not detach the correction quotation or use destroyed nations to decide any later identity.

route.title: Judicial wait and assembly pivot
route.marker: Therefore-wait-for-me gathers the preceding failed correction into a judicial assembly declaration; the for-then expression at Zeph.3.9 turns from judgment to purified speech and service.
route.rationale: Zephaniah 3:8 is exposed as a judicial hinge because it gathers failed correction into assembly and fire before 3:9 turns to purification; parent hydration protects both dependencies.
route.counter: The verse depends strongly on both neighboring movements and must never surface without the Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13 parent.
route.basis: Its inferential opening, wait summons, assembly language, and judgment culmination make it a recoverable pivot, while the causal-temporal turn at 3:9 begins the resulting promise movement.
route.guard: Never isolate the assembly-and-fire pivot as a universal destruction chronology; hydrate Zeph.3.8-3.13.

route.title: Purified peoples and dispersed worshipers
route.marker: The for-then turn develops purified speech, joint service, and dispersed worshipers through Zeph.3.10; the in-that-day formula and renewed feminine-singular city address begin a distinct remnant movement at 3:11.
route.rationale: Purified speech, shared service, and dispersed worshipers form the first promise child, ending where the in-that-day formula and city address reset the discourse.
route.counter: Purification, pride removal, and remnant formation remain one larger restoration sequence, so the canonical lane's whole Zeph.3.9-Zeph.3.13 surface remains a defensible dissent.
route.basis: The causal-temporal opening, peoples-oriented purification and service, and dispersed-worshiper continuation form a dependent promise child; the temporal and address reset at 3:11 is strong enough to expose the next child separately.
route.guard: Do not treat purified speech or dispersed worshipers as a standalone identity or soteriology definition.

route.title: Humble and secure remnant
route.marker: The in-that-day formula and city address introduce removal of pride and the remaining humble people; truthful speech, rest, and safety close before the WLC-family samekh after Zeph.3.13.
route.rationale: Proud removal and the humble remnant belong together through truthful speech, rest, safety, and marked closure; merging backward would erase the 3:11 address turn.
route.counter: The unit is causally continuous with purification in 3:9-10 and cannot be treated as an independent identity proposition.
route.basis: Temporal and address reset, remnant focus, coordinated character-and-security description, and marked closure converge on this child unit.
route.guard: Do not detach the remnant description as an ethnic, ecclesial, political, or total identity proposition.

route.title: Zion song and divine rejoicing
route.marker: Song imperatives at Zeph.3.14 develop through removed judgments, royal presence, the fear-not reassurance reported at 3:16, saving presence, and divine rejoicing through 3:17.
route.rationale: The reported reassurance at 3:16 supplies the Zion song with its saving-presence ground, so it remains an internal speech seam within the complete rejoicing movement.
route.counter: The in-that-day report at 3:16 is a genuine internal speech seam and supports the canonical lane's proposed child division.
route.basis: The reported reassurance at 3:16 develops the song's grounds for rejoicing rather than starting a new oracle; royal and saving presence unites 3:15-17.
route.guard: Do not isolate the rejoicing language as an unconditional prosperity, security, or fulfillment promise.

route.title: Closing restoration and return
route.marker: The difficult first-person collection language at Zeph.3.18 proceeds into explicit rescue, gathering, praise, and return language and closes with the says-Yahweh formula at 3:20.
route.rationale: Difficult 3:18 wording is kept with rescue, gathering, praise, return, and the final speech formula, preserving a closing restoration unit without settling its translation.
route.rejected: Attach Zeph.3.18 to Zeph.3.14-Zeph.3.17; Zeph.3.19-Zeph.3.20; Detach Zeph.3.20 as an isolated promise
route.counter: The syntax and subject scope of Zeph.3.18 are difficult and may connect backward to the song or its festal setting; this lowers confidence but does not presently require a boundary hold.
route.basis: First-person collection, rescue, gathering, praise, return, and the terminal speech formula support a closing restoration movement while avoiding a preferred resolution of Zeph.3.18's syntax.
route.guard: Do not turn gathering, praise, return, or restored fortunes into an unqualified promise to a later nation, church, or individual.

dissents.rationale: The samekh after 2:4 and fresh woe at 2:5 preserve a dependent child seam even though the coast judgment and remnant reversal remain the surfaced unit.
The one-verse Cush oracle is recoverable by address and geographic turn but remains unsafe without the Zeph.2.4-2.15 nations-cycle parent.
Judgment, purification, and remnant outcomes form one coherent parent despite surfacing the 3:8 pivot and two dependent promise children.
The canonical lane retains one causal purification-and-remnant movement; the boss selected the 3:11 temporal and address seam without erasing this dissent.
The reported reassurance at 3:16 is a genuine child seam even though royal and saving presence unifies the surfaced song.
Difficult syntax and subject scope at 3:18 preserve possible backward attachment without selecting a preferred translation or creating a boundary hold.
